description: Organization-wide Renovate policy for liverty-music, inherited by every repository in the org.

Renovate auto-discovers this file in the org's .github repository, so a policy change here takes effect everywhere without editing each repository. Per-repository renovate.json files add only what is specific to their stack.

Built by extending config:best-practices rather than assembling rules by hand: a locally copied group does not learn about packages added upstream later, so it narrows silently while continuing to look correct. See the OpenSpec change `automate-dependency-updates`, design D14.

The recurring human actions this policy implies — regenerating visual baselines after a Playwright bump, reviewing a Pulumi preview, handling an urgent fix held by the release-age delay, updating buf.lock by hand — are documented in renovate-runbook.md next to this file.

The observation cycle this schedule was briefly lifted for is complete. It corrected four assumptions that could only be checked by running Renovate: `group:pulumi` does NOT group the Pulumi providers (they are grouped locally now, as noise reduction — they are not version-coupled); BSR-generated Go modules cannot be looked up at all; our own container images were being proposed for update, which would have been a deployment; and `helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests` was pinning our OWN reusable workflow, severing the `@main` reference it depends on. What the cycle CONFIRMED: `group:monorepos` works for Vitest, OpenTelemetry JS and the Node family (`node` + `@types/node` in one pull request), the Playwright custom manager matches all three of its locations, and Aurelia stays on `2.0.0-rc.2` without a local rule — so none was written.

packageRules.description: Release-age delay, stated explicitly so it survives a schedule change. config:best-practices brings security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm, which covers npm only; these are the other datasources this org automerges, and each is equally reachable by a compromised maintainer account. NOTE: this delay is NOT bypassed for vulnerability fixes. Renovate's vulnerability path ignores schedule and the concurrency limits, but not minimumReleaseAge. That is deliberate and left as-is: a delay exists precisely because a release claiming to be a security fix can itself be the attack. A genuinely urgent fix is merged by hand — see the runbook.
Monthly cadence for the slow-moving, high-fan-out axes. Weekly proposals for these produce churn out of proportion to how often they actually matter.
schedule: before 6am on the first day of the month

packageRules.description: Keep @biomejs/biome on one cadence across the org. frontend and cloud-provisioning pin it to the same exact version, and Renovate cannot group across repositories — so the two will always be two pull requests. Putting the schedule here rather than in each repository's config is what keeps them landing close together: a per-repo schedule change could silently desynchronise the formatter, and a formatter mismatch rewrites files on every save.

Do NOT pin liverty-music's own Actions and reusable workflows to a SHA. `helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests` (from config:best-practices) pins every `uses:` reference it finds, and it caught `liverty-music/.github/.github/workflows/claude-review.yml@main` in all three repositories that consume it. That reference is `@main` deliberately: the whole point of a reusable workflow is that fixing it in one place reaches every consumer, and freezing it to a SHA severs exactly that. The security argument for pinning does not apply either — pinning protects against a third party repointing a tag at code we have not read, and this is our own code under our own review. The capability states the exemption directly: "Actions published from within the liverty-music organization are exempt, as their contents are already under this project's control."

PERMANENT: the .github repository never automerges. It has no GitHubRepositoryComponent in cloud-provisioning, so it has no branch protection, no required status checks and no CI of its own — an automerge there would land with no gate whatsoever, which is the opposite of the policy this configuration implements. Renovate still raises pull requests for its GitHub Actions; a human merges them. Removing this rule requires first giving .github its own CI and protection (design D11, follow-up 12.4).
